title: Mercy's hundred parts
hookLine: Allah made mercy in a hundred parts and sent down one

cards: A horse stands over her newborn foal in the straw. She shifts her weight, and before her hoof comes down, she lifts it, carefully, so it doesn't land on the little one. A small thing.
If you've watched animals with their young, you may have seen moves like it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, pointed to exactly that moment, and said it comes from somewhere.

teach.h: ONE PART SENT DOWN, NINETY-NINE KEPT.
teach.b: Here's the hadith, from Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase. Allah made mercy in a hundred parts.

teach.h: ALL KINDNESS ON EARTH IS ONE PART.
teach.b: He kept ninety-nine with Himself, and sent one part down to the earth. From that one part, all creation shows mercy to each other, so much that the mare lifts her hoof away from her foal, afraid of hurting it.

teach.h: THE NINETY-NINE, KEPT FOR THAT DAY.
teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, a version adds where the ninety-nine are kept: for the Day of Resurrection, to be shown to His servants then. Sit with the arithmetic. Every kindness you've ever seen comes from one part.
A parent up in the night with a sick child. A stranger who held the door. A nurse who stayed after her shift.
The mare and her hoof. All of it together is a hundredth. Now look at where this lands in the path.
For days we've walked the unseen: death, the grave, the gathering, the scale, the bridge, the fire. What will that Day be like? Ninety-nine parts of mercy are being kept for it.

The Qur'an says it too, in Pickthall's translation: "My mercy embraceth all things." Some Muslim teachers hold the warnings and the mercy side by side, so that neither fear nor hope swallows the other.
And the one part was sent down to be used. Every time someone is gentle, that part is moving through the world, and the next kind thing you do is a small piece of it.

how: Some Muslim teachers cite the hadith of mercy's hundred parts alongside descriptions of the Day of Judgment, so that hope and fear are held together; Muslims call on Allah as ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim, the names in the bismillah.

games.why: the hadith names that small lifted hoof as a sign of the one part of mercy sent to earth.

practice: Bring to mind someone who could use a little gentleness from you, maybe someone you've been short with, or someone carrying a lot.
Choose one act of mercy, a softer tone, a message, patience with a slow answer, forgiving a small debt, and let it be as careful as the mare lifting her hoof.
If you pray, call on Allah as ar-Rahman, ar-Rahim; if not, simply hold the person in mind with care.

wordCard.voice: Mercy's hundred parts. One part sent down, from which all creatures are kind to each other, and ninety-nine kept with Allah for the Day. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: mercy; the word the hadith divides into a hundred parts.

carryVoice: Your line: ninety-nine kept for that day. One part is already here, in every kindness. That's today, done.
